scope: F07 decoy isolation: the C12 decoy handler runs inside a rootless container that has no network at all, no capabilities, no host namespace and a read-only root filesystem, bounded by a hard process and memory limit. The supervisor states the policy, the limited container provider applies it and the supervisor verifies the observed and the effective controls before it reports a running decoy. The engine starts the isolated decoy with --decoy-isolation and propagates the typed outcome.
owner_scope_resolution: The owner approved the internal decoy isolation on the C13 card targets, a test only decoy host that runs the real C12 handler inside the container, the image locked by full digest with its provenance and licenses recorded, a minimal runtime workflow preparation, and a minimal extension of the C12 anchor. The reviews required the mount roles bound to the fixed container targets, the immutability of the validated policy, the verification of the exact and the effective runtime controls, the reporting of a failed cleanup, the wiring of the typed outcome into the supported engine workflow, a digest pinned image with no implicit pull, the cancellation of the runtime calls, a bounded capture of the runtime output, the use of the versioned expected outcome fixture, the rollback of a container that an uncertain start may have created, the signals of the operator in the workflow and the explicit removal before the outcome is written. All of them are implemented and each one is proved by a mutation and a regression. At the original C13 implementation handoff, no commit, push or publication was requested or performed; the owner later requested the bc84ea6 follow-up commit. The last review required that the runtime copies no proxy setting of the host into the decoy, that the command fails when it cannot deliver its typed result and that the restart regression compares the exact number of the stored observations. All three are implemented, proved by a regression and recorded in the evidence.

acceptance_checks.acceptance: Decoy cannot call Internet or operational private subnets; PID and memory limits hold.
acceptance_checks.evidence: TestDecoyIsolationDeniesInternetAndPrivateSubnets starts the real C12 handler inside the isolated container and proves three things with the real provider. First the container has no route: the probe reports zero routes in /proc/net/route and every direct outbound attempt answers network is unreachable, for 1.1.1.1:80, 8.8.8.8:53, 10.0.0.1:80, 172.16.0.1:80 and 192.168.0.1:80. Second the decoy itself still works: the probe reaches the C12 handler on the loopback of the container and the observation lands in the durable C05 store on the host. Third the container is unprivileged: the effective and the bounding capability set of the process are both empty, the runtime reports the dropped capabilities, the read-only root filesystem and the privilege protection. The inherited proxy settings of the operator are cleared inside the container, so an egress attempt cannot be tunnelled through them. TestDecoyIsolationEnforcesPIDAndMemoryLimits proves the limits with the real cgroup: pids.max is the policy value, memory.max is the policy value, memory.swap.max is 0, a fork storm is refused with the process limit and an allocation above the limit is killed, which the cgroup memory.events oom_kill counter records, while the decoy keeps serving. The observed results are compared with the versioned fixture tests/fixtures/miragemesh/C13/expected-output.json, so the declared outcomes cannot drift. The engine workflow starts the isolated decoy with --decoy-isolation, verifies the observed and the effective controls, removes the container again and writes the typed outcome only after the removal succeeded.

negative_case_checks.case: Missing prerequisites, malformed fixtures or unavailable required providers produce an explicit error rather than placeholder success.
negative_case_checks.evidence: TestDecoyIsolationProviderFailuresAreExplicit drives the provider: a missing runtime binary returns decoy.ErrProviderUnavailable, an image that is not present locally returns the explicit missing image error and a runtime that reports a non rootless host returns the explicit not rootless error. The provider never pulls an image and every run refuses an implicit pull, so a missing image cannot be fetched silently. TestDecoyIsolationPolicyRejectsUnsafeConfiguration covers the twenty-four fixture rows: an empty image, a mutable tag, an empty command, a requested egress posture, a root user, a named root user, a missing memory limit, a missing process limit, a relative mount, a writable artifact, an extra writable mount, an unknown mount role, a duplicate mount target, a proxy setting, an invalid container name, a missing artifact mount, a missing state mount, a wrong artifact target, a wrong state target, a read-only state and an extra mount all return decoy.ErrInvalidPolicy, and no supervisor is returned. The provider checks the host side of the mounts as well: the artifact must be a regular file and the state must be a directory. A runtime that cannot apply the memory limit fails the policy verification instead of reporting the limit as held.

negative_case_checks.case: Repeat after restart and verify the declared invariant and documented recovery outcome.
negative_case_checks.evidence: TestDecoyIsolationReconcilesAfterRestart starts a decoy, sends a real C12 request through the first container, then a second supervisor with the same container name starts again: the container of the earlier supervisor is gone, the new container has a different identity and the policy is verified again. After the replacement is stopped the same C05 store is reopened and the observation of the first container is still there, with its path and its sequence, and the store holds exactly the number of observations the fixture declares, so a duplicate would fail the regression. A decoy container is never reused across supervisor restarts; the durable state lives outside the container in the C05 store. TestDecoyIsolationStopsAndRemovesItsContainer proves that the stop removes the container and that a second stop is not an error, so the cleanup leaves no leaked runtime resource behind. TestDecoyIsolationReportsCleanupFailure proves that a removal that fails is reported together with the failure that caused it, so a container that stayed behind is never hidden.

The policy admits only the denied egress posture, so no configuration can ask for outbound access, and the adapter always passes the network none argument, the private namespaces, the dropped capabilities, the privilege protection, the read-only root filesystem, the unprivileged user and the cleared proxy settings. The container of the decoy has no interface and no route, so neither the Internet nor an operational private subnet is reachable. TestDecoyIsolationAdapterRunsOnlyTheContainerRuntime keeps the one new permission limited: the isolation adapter is the only package that may run another program, it may use os/exec for the container runtime and nothing else, and it may not use a network client or a shell.

security_review.verification: The supervisor compares the observed runtime state with the policy before it reports a decoy: the state, the network mode, the requested limits, the read-only root filesystem, the user, the privilege protection and the capability sets. It compares the effective controls as well: the effective and the bounding capability set of the container process must be empty and the control group of the container must carry the process limit and the memory limit of the policy with a swap limit of zero. A mismatch removes the container and reports an explicit failure, so an unverified decoy is never reported.
security_review.atomicity: One container is started per supervisor. The sequence of reconcile, start, wait and verify is bounded: the supervisor waits for the running state and reports the state it reached when the container leaves it.
security_review.data_bounds: The decoy handler keeps its C12 bounds inside the container: the request size, the path length and the version 1 event payload limit are unchanged, and the durable store keeps its own quotas. The adapter keeps at most one MiB of the output of a runtime call and drops the rest while the call continues, so a noisy runtime cannot grow the memory of the engine.
security_review.egress: The container has no network namespace interface, no route and no resolver. The operator proxy settings are cleared inside the container, so a denied attempt cannot be tunnelled. The runtime copies no proxy setting of the host into the container at all: the run arguments carry --http-proxy=false and every proxy variable is explicitly emptied, so a host proxy URL or credential never reaches the decoy process. The decoy package itself still cannot dial out: the C12 anchor is unchanged and still rejects every net/http identifier that is not a handler API.
security_review.privileges: The container runs with all capabilities dropped, no new privileges, a read-only root filesystem, an unprivileged user and private IPC, UTS, PID and cgroup namespaces. The effective capability set of the process is zero.
security_review.filesystem: The decoy artifact is mounted read-only at the fixed target /usr/local/bin/decoy and the durable state is mounted writable at the fixed target /var/lib/miragemesh, at the identity of the operator, so the C05 ownership and mode rules keep holding inside and outside the container. A policy accepts exactly these two roles and targets, the provider checks that the artifact is a regular file and the state is a directory, and the engine prepares the state directory and refuses one that is not private to its owner. A policy can therefore never expose an unrelated host path to the decoy.
security_review.known_limits: The local clock and the private store remain trusted. The container has no inbound path, so the decoy is not published to untrusted peers; that is later workflow work. A rootless runtime without cgroup delegation cannot apply the memory limit and fails the verification instead of reporting the limit as held. The engine workflow verifies one isolated decoy and removes it again; it does not keep a decoy running.

observed_limitations: No decoy surface is published: the container has no network at all, so the decoy address is reachable only from inside its own namespace. Publishing the decoy to untrusted peers with the outbound denial kept is later workflow work.
The engine workflow verifies one isolated decoy and removes it again; it does not keep a decoy running. A persistent decoy service is later workflow work.
The memory limit needs a rootless runtime with cgroup delegation. A runtime without it fails the policy verification; the limit is never reported as held because it was requested.
The provider is the only place that runs another program. It runs the container runtime with a fixed argument vector, without a shell and without a network client, and it never pulls an image.

The pinned image is not redistributed by MirageMesh. Its digest, platform, provenance and the license of every component are recorded in docs/engineering/toolchain-lock.json; the image contains a GPL-2.0-only busybox component, which the operator accepts by pulling it.

The decoy host of the tests is a test fixture, not a product listener: it exists so that the real C12 handler runs under the isolation policy and so that the probes measure the isolation from inside the container. The decoy artifact of the engine workflow is supplied by the operator; the decoy service binary is later work.

The state directory of the workflow must be writable by the operator: a rootless installation cannot write into /var/lib, so the examples use a user owned path and the engine refuses a state path that is not a private directory of the owner.

rollback_or_recovery_observation: The change adds a new package, a new decoy file and a test fixture. Reverting them removes the isolation and leaves the C12 decoy untouched. A running decoy container is removed by the supervisor; a container left behind by an earlier run is removed by the next start. The durable observations live outside the container in the C05 store, so they survive a restart and must be preserved like any other accepted event.
